svg.title: Laminar and turbulent flow
svg.desc: (a) Laminar flow over a smooth fixed surface: the fluid moves right in layers that do not mix. The top layer moves fastest, at vt, and each layer below is slower, down to vb next to the surface, because friction acts between the layers and with the surface. (b) An obstruction on the bottom makes the flow turbulent: streamlines that start out smooth break into swirling eddies over and behind it. The fluid approaches at speed v both near the top and near the bottom. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.
